thread:
sec-alert-bot: [ALERT] Suspicious hostPath mount detected on pod 'cfg-syncer-7f9b2' in cluster-prod-us-west1. Rule: runtime-hostpath-write-high
sanjay: Seeing the alert. Which node is this on? Any execs/restarts?
morgan: kubectl -n infra get pod cfg-syncer-7f9b2 -o wide
morgan: ```
NAME              READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP           NODE                NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
cfg-syncer-7f9b2  1/1     Running   0          3h   10.2.14.87   prod-node-04        <none>           <none>
``` 
morgan: kubectl -n infra describe pod cfg-syncer-7f9b2 | grep -A2 "Mounts"
morgan: ```
Mounts:
  /etc/secret-config from host-config (rw,path="/etc/customer-config")
``` 
kai: hostPath -> /etc/customer-config is unusual. That directory contains KMS config symlinks. :eyes:
jamie: @elaine @sanjay can you check KMS access logs for any decrypt requests around 13:02-13:10 UTC?
elaine: I'm on it. Pulling logs from key-a. Quick grep:
elaine: ```
2026-03-19T13:05:12Z key-a decrypt caller=serviceAccount:infra-syncer@prod.svc.cluster.local result=OK requestId=ckm-9a1b
2026-03-19T13:05:13Z key-a decrypt caller=unknown result=DENIED requestId=ckm-9a2c
``` 
sanjay: There's one successful decrypt by infra-syncer SA. The unknown DENIED is weird but not successful.
morgan: Any execs into the pod? kube-audit snippet:
morgan: ```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-19T13:04:58Z","user":"system:serviceaccount:infra:infra-syncer","verb":"create","resource":"exec"}
``` 
kai: Looks like an exec request was issued by the pod's SA. Could be legitimate syncer behavior, but hostPath exposes config — risk of exfil.
jamie: I'd recommend immediate containment: cordon node prod-node-04, evict pod, snapshot host path, rotate KMS keys for affected key material, and block outbound for that node until investigation.
sanjay: Agreed. Oncall @morgan, can you cordon and bring node to maintenance mode? Also take a node-level memory/process snapshot (gcore) if possible.
morgan: Cordon + drain started:
morgan: ```
kubectl cordon prod-node-04 && kubectl drain prod-node-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
``` 
morgan: Started gcore via ssh, copying /etc/customer-config to secure bucket (read-only snapshot). :lock: 
elaine: KMS key rotation scheduled for 13:20 UTC. Will rotate and issue new keys to services after validation. Will also open KMS audit ticket.
jamie: Security pager duty notified. Creating incident ticket I-20260319-42 and assigning to eng-security + infra.
sec-alert-bot: Incident I-20260319-42 created. Attach logs: alert-log, pod-describe, node-proc-snapshot.
kai: Short-term mitigations: revoke infra-syncer SA tokens, recreate SA with least-privs, apply PodSecurityPolicy denying hostPath for infra namespace, add audit webhook to capture hostPath mounts.
sanjay: We should also check image signatures and verify digest for cfg-syncer image.
morgan: `docker image inspect registry.redwood/cfg-syncer:sha256:abcd1234` -> image labels show build host ci-builder-01. No suspicious layers but we'll run an offline scan.
elaine: From KMS logs, only key-a saw one successful decrypt from infra-syncer. No external IPs observed contacting node during window. Network egress logs are attached.
jamie: Action items:
- morgan: node snapshot + image scan + preserve pod logs (ETA 1h)
- elaine: KMS rotation + audit ticket (ETA 30m)
- kai: policy changes + PSP enforcement (ETA 2d)
- sanjay: postmortem + timeline (ETA EOD)
sanjay: We'll treat this as potential exfil until scan proves otherwise. Keep comms in thread, do not post external details.
morgan: Quick note: pulled file list from /etc/customer-config: contains symlink to /var/run/kv-cache and a mounted conf.json with credentials. Adding to evidence.
kai: Recommend immediate RBAC hardening: remove create/exec on pods for infra-syncer SA and restrict to specific pods with PodSecurity context.
jamie: We'll schedule a follow-up post-incident review with infra and platform next Wed. For now, I'll update I-20260319-42 with containment steps and notify legal if we find any data leakage.
elaine: KMS rotation done. New key id: key-a-rot-20260319. Old key disabled pending forensic review.
sanjay: Thanks all. Keep thread updated. If anyone finds confirmed indicators of compromise, escalate to Incident Commander.
morgan: :fire_extinguisher: node cordoned, pod evicted, artifacts uploaded to secure bucket under s3://redwood-sec/investigations/I-20260319-42/
sec-alert-bot: Reaction recorded: :lock: from @sec-team
jamie: Closing checklist for now: evidence preserved, access tokens revoked, node isolated. Will remain open until scans complete. :heavy_check_mark:
